title: Bhooth Bangla Has Crossed Sooryavanshi Worldwide. Akshay Kumar Now Has His Second-Highest Post-COVID Grosser.
excerpt: The horror-comedy has quietly climbed past ₹200 crore worldwide in seven weeks, overtaking one of Akshay Kumar's most celebrated pandemic-era hits.
body:
Bhooth Bangla, the Akshay Kumar-led horror comedy, has now crossed the worldwide collections of Sooryavanshi in its seventh week of release. The milestone makes it Akshay Kumar's second-highest-grossing film in the post-COVID era, trailing only behind OMG 2 among his recent releases.

The Quiet Climb

Unlike Sooryavanshi, which arrived with massive Diwali fanfare and a Rohit Shetty-scale marketing blitz in 2021, Bhooth Bangla has done its work through sustained word-of-mouth and family audience pull. The film has crossed the ₹200 crore worldwide gross mark — a number that would have been routine for Akshay Kumar a decade ago but has become genuinely significant given the turbulent stretch his career has endured since the pandemic.

Between 2022 and 2025, Akshay Kumar released a string of underperformers: Samrat Prithviraj, Raksha Bandhan, Ram Setu, Selfiee, Mission Raniganj, Bade Miyan Chote Miyan, Sarfira, and Khel Khel Mein — a run of commercial misfires that prompted serious conversation about whether the Khiladi era was over. Bhooth Bangla has not ended that conversation entirely, but it has paused it. The film's seven-week run in theatres — during a period when most Hindi films struggle to hold screens past ten days — is a statement in itself.

Why Horror-Comedy Worked

The genre has been quietly reliable in Hindi cinema for the past five years. Stree, Stree 2, Bhediya, and Munjya proved that Indian audiences will turn up for horror-comedies that balance scares with humor, especially when the casting is right and the budget is disciplined. Bhooth Bangla follows this playbook without attempting to reinvent it.

Akshay Kumar in a horror-comedy is not a natural fit on paper — he has built his brand on patriotic dramas, action films, and social-message vehicles. But the shift toward lighter, crowd-pleasing material appears to have reconnected him with the mass family audience that had drifted away during his prestige-film phase.

The Box-Office Context

To put the Sooryavanshi comparison in perspective: Sooryavanshi earned approximately ₹195 crore in India net and around ₹290 crore worldwide when it released in November 2021, as the first major Hindi film to arrive after the second COVID lockdown. It was an event release — audiences were starved for a theatre experience, and Sooryavanshi benefited from pent-up demand as much as from Rohit Shetty's brand.

Bhooth Bangla has achieved its milestone under very different conditions. It released in a crowded marketplace alongside Ram Charan's Peddi and other major titles, without the event-release premium. That it has overtaken Sooryavanshi's worldwide total speaks to the kind of sustained daily collections that only word-of-mouth-driven hits generate.

What This Means for Akshay Kumar's Career

The more important question for NRI audiences who grew up on Akshay Kumar's films is whether Bhooth Bangla represents a genuine career reset or a one-off reprieve. The answer likely lies somewhere in between. The film's success does not erase the years of underperformance, but it does demonstrate that the audience for Akshay Kumar's particular brand of mainstream entertainment still exists — it had simply stopped finding what it wanted in his recent choices.

His upcoming slate includes several films in various stages of production, and the lesson from Bhooth Bangla is clear: genre discipline, controlled budgets, and commercial instincts beat ambitious prestige plays when the market has already moved on from your peak stardom.

The Diaspora Perspective

For Indian families abroad, Akshay Kumar remains one of the defining Bollywood stars of the 2000s and 2010s. His decline had been a frequent topic of conversation among diaspora film communities. Bhooth Bangla will not restore his commercial peak, but it offers something more useful: proof that there is a floor beneath the fall, and that floor is higher than most of his contemporaries can reach on their best day.

The film continues to trickle in daily collections as it enters its eighth week. An OTT release is expected within the next few weeks, which will extend its reach significantly among diaspora audiences who may have missed it in theatres.
